name: Sriharsha
bio: Sriharsha (Shriharsha) was a Sanskrit poet and philosopher of the twelfth century, court poet to a king of Kanyakubja (Kannauj). By his own account in the colophons of his poem he was the son of Shrihira and Mamalladevi.

His best-known work is the Naishadhiyacharita, a learned court epic in twenty-two cantos on the love of King Nala of Nishadha and Damayanti of Vidarbha, famed for its verbal virtuosity. He also wrote the philosophical treatise Khandanakhandakhadya, a defence of Advaita Vedanta.
